status: three full-cover trials requested; no final typography approval
user_request: My favourite is H, followed by A and E. Let's try full covers in those three.
controls: Independent edits of chosen 06B; one chosen family throughout each. Actual font specimens supplied directly. Background, photograph, border and sticker composition retained. Title spacing/scale may adapt to natural glyph proportions; no invented G swash.
limitations: Native image edits are guided by actual font specimens; exact font embedding and pixel identity are not guaranteed.

variants.name: Lilita One
variants.direction: FONT H — LILITA ONE, the user's first choice and the interior heading font. Faithfully follow IMAGE 2: chunky friendly sans-serif display letters, softly rounded corners, distinctive compact counters and terminals, robust consistent stroke weight. Use the authentic Lilita shapes, not a rounded retro serif, not Cooper Black and not generic bubble lettering. There must be NO serifs or curled serif-style G tail. Carry these same distinctive letters into the sticker and author credit; smaller type stays Lilita, never a neutral sans substitute.
variants.prompt:
Create ONE complete, flat, portrait front-cover design by editing IMAGE 1, using the actual font shapes supplied in IMAGE 2.

REFERENCE ROLES:
IMAGE 1 is authoritative for the chosen LIGHTER SAGE colour, photograph, clean rectangular photo crop, offset composition, broad left field, visible right border, circular subtitle sticker overlapping the lower-left photo corner, and author position. Preserve these.
IMAGE 2 is an actual typeset specimen of the user's chosen font. It is authoritative ONLY for the letterforms and font weight, for ALL text on this cover. Do not copy its white background, green title colour, specimen layout or line arrangements.

FONT H — LILITA ONE, the user's first choice and the interior heading font. Faithfully follow IMAGE 2: chunky friendly sans-serif display letters, softly rounded corners, distinctive compact counters and terminals, robust consistent stroke weight. Use the authentic Lilita shapes, not a rounded retro serif, not Cooper Black and not generic bubble lettering. There must be NO serifs or curled serif-style G tail. ONE TYPEFACE THROUGHOUT: Use this chosen family for the complete title, the small upright "The", the subtitle in the circle, and "John Lennon". Do not mix fonts anywhere. Respect the natural glyph shapes shown in IMAGE 2. Do not copy the old cover's serif letterforms into a sans-serif trial. Do not invent a swash or long curled G tail where the chosen font does not have one.

TITLE COMPOSITION: Keep the striking, oversized warm cream title crossing the left edge of the photograph: small "The" at top, "Vegetable" on one broad line across the upper portion, and "Guru" below at the left. The V and G should still bridge the sage field and the photograph. Adapt their scale and spacing with design judgement to the selected font's natural proportions; no artificial horizontal stretching, no old decorative serif tail. Preserve strong hierarchy and the adventurous spill across the photo boundary. Keep John's face fully clear and the title out of the tomatoes and hands. Do not shrink this into a conventional small title block.

SUBTITLE: Keep the existing cream circular sticker, same size and lower-left position, partly on and partly off the photograph. Its dark-green wording must be in the SAME chosen font, legible and comfortably contained, with these four centred lines:
Your
at-a-glance
growing
companion

AUTHOR: Keep "John Lennon" in dark green at bottom right, using the SAME chosen font as all other wording, in a balanced size fitting that footer.

FIXED VISUALS: Preserve the exact light sage appearance from IMAGE 1: no darker green, olive, mint, mustard, yellow or blue. Preserve the cream title and sticker, dark-green supporting wording, subtle surface finish, generous right margin and rectangular photo. Do not change John's face, expression, age, hair, beard, checked shirt, olive T-shirt, hands, colander, red tomatoes or greenhouse foliage. No new objects or retouching.

Exact cover wording appears once each:
The Vegetable Guru
Your at-a-glance growing companion
John Lennon

Output the complete cover only, in the same portrait proportions as IMAGE 1. No font names, labels, sample headings, variant letters, mockup perspective or extra claims in the artwork.
